title: cite-check-downstream-pr
summary: Review a downstream PR description for correct acceptance issue links, SHA pins, and artifact citations.

skill_metadata.name: cite-check-downstream-pr
skill_metadata.description: Review a downstream PR description for correct acceptance issue links, SHA pins, and artifact citations.

applicability.scope: Review of a downstream PR description that cites RSI acceptance work for a performance or quality improvement
applicability.prerequisites: The PR description, the acceptance issue it cites, and the evidence paths it names; reviewing is read-only and needs no local run
applicability.input_contract: One PR description plus the cited acceptance issue and its evidence tree; the reviewer reads claims and citations, not the candidate code
applicability.produced_artifact: A per-checklist review result that either accepts the citation or marks the summary unverified, using only PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE vocabulary
failure_modes: No acceptance issue URL, only a chat thread
Branch names instead of full baseline and candidate SHAs
Microbenchmark evidence offered for an end-to-end latency claim
A threshold restated or invented relative to the acceptance issue
Evidence path absent, stale or on a different SHA than the cited candidate
applicability.refusal_point: Refuses to restate a performance or quality claim whose artifacts are missing, stale or off-SHA; reports the summary as unverified instead

recommendations: Read the cited acceptance issue before the PR description so an invented threshold is visible immediately.
Resolve every listed evidence path and compare its SHA with the candidate SHA the PR names.
Report an unverifiable claim as unverified rather than repeating its number.
limitations: Checklist-only procedure; it validates citation discipline, not the measurement behind an artifact.
A passing review does not establish that the campaign evidence itself is correct.
skill_metadata.searchspace_not_applicable: SKILL.md §§ Checklist and Red flags check acceptance links, revision/artifact citations and claim wording; they provide no hardware-resource mechanism.
